allowed_fields: FY2024 and FY2023-comparable tungsten-molybdenum reportable-segment revenue and reported segment operating profit
hard-alloy, cutting-tool, and fine-tungsten-wire sales volumes using the frozen product definitions
external main-business gross margin using the same definition as FY2023
only segment-attributed equity-method income, disposal gains, non-persistent subsidies, other one-offs, and reversals needed to reconstruct adjusted recurring segment profit
segment capital expenditure, depreciation and amortization, asset impairment, and utilization where disclosed
product-level recurring unit economics after persistent R&D, selling, administrative, and capital burden only where explicitly attributable
segment perimeter, internal-elimination, product-definition, or accounting changes needed for comparability
cells.calculation_rule: Reconstruct SEGMENT_ATTRIBUTED_ADJUSTED_RECURRING_PROFIT from the comparable reported segment profit. Remove or add back only an item with explicit tungsten-molybdenum segment attribution. Never allocate a group equity-method, subsidy, disposal, or impairment amount to this segment without such evidence.

allowed_fields: FY2024 and FY2023-comparable revenue and reported segment operating profit for battery materials and rare earth separately
battery key sales volume defined as ternary material plus lithium cobalt oxide and rare-earth key sales volume defined as rare-earth oxide plus rare-earth metal plus magnetic material

only segment-attributed disposal gains, non-persistent subsidies, non-operating investment income, consolidation one-offs, and reversible non-operating losses needed to reconstruct each adjusted recurring segment profit
capital expenditure, depreciation and amortization, asset impairment, and utilization for each segment separately
segment perimeter, business-transfer, internal-elimination, product-definition, or accounting changes needed for comparability
cells.calculation_rule: Reconstruct battery-materials and rare-earth adjusted recurring segment profit independently before aggregation. Do not let one segment's unallocated item or profit mechanically offset the other, and do not allocate group items without segment evidence.

allowed_fields: cash paid to acquire fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets
comparable interest-bearing debt consisting of short-term borrowings, current maturities, long-term borrowings, and bonds payable

material non-wholly-owned subsidiary post-capex cash, NCI economic claims, mandatory retention or reinvestment, actual recurring dividends or lawful upstream cash received by the parent, and net parent cash support where disclosed
legal, regulatory, minority-shareholder, or financing-contract restrictions on upstream cash
cash-flow classification, acquisition, disposal, restricted-cash, perimeter, or debt-definition changes needed for comparability

formulas.group_cash_proxy: consolidated operating cash flow minus cash paid to acquire fixed assets, intangible assets and other long-term assets
formulas.parent_distributable_owner_cash: material non-wholly-owned subsidiary post-capex cash minus NCI claims and required retention or reinvestment, reconciled to recurring parent receipts and net parent support; disposal, borrowing and capital return are excluded

output_requirements: Record every raw reported value, unit, responsibility boundary, printed page, and source locator before each derived value.
Apply the frozen first-match in order and identify the matched class for every cell.
Keep tungsten-molybdenum, battery materials, and rare earth on separate responsibility boundaries before any aggregation.
Do not allocate group investment income, subsidy, disposal, impairment, or other one-off items to a segment without explicit segment attribution.
Keep group cash, NCI claims, parent access, and permanent-loss carriers separate; an open parent bridge must not erase an observed group cash direction.
Keep UNKNOWN and measurement mismatch local and continue settling every other observable cell.
Do not infer management quality, enterprise conclusions, training utility, valuation, price, return, or investment action.
